cfb-2017-09-02-wnmu-usd: San Diego opened its 2017 season with a 34–20 victory over Western New Mexico at Torero Stadium, overcoming a 13–0 first-quarter deficit. The Mustangs struck first behind [[cfb-wnmu-javia-hall|Javia Hall]], but [[cfb-usd-anthony-lawrence|Anthony Lawrence]] immediately connected with [[cfb-usd-justin-priest|Justin Priest]] for a 58-yard touchdown. The Toreros added a field goal before the quarter ended, then took a 17–13 halftime lead and eventually scored 27 unanswered points.

Lawrence finished 15-for-28 for 187 yards and two touchdowns, including a two-yard scoring pass to Ross Dwelley in the third quarter. Freshman [[cfb-usd-emilio-martinez|Emilio Martinez]] ran 17 times for 96 yards and sealed the win with a 13-yard touchdown after Western New Mexico cut the lead to 27–20 in the fourth. Priest caught four passes for 95 yards and a score, while [[cfb-usd-kim-mahoney|Kim Mahoney]] contributed eight tackles as San Diego recovered five Mustang fumbles.

Western New Mexico actually outgained San Diego 506–339. Hall threw for 464 yards and three touchdowns, while [[cfb-wnmu-d-angelo-bowie|D'Angelo Bowie]] caught 19 passes for 263 yards and two scores, including an 86-yard fourth-quarter touchdown. The Toreros' five takeaways proved decisive in a game where the visitors produced more yardage but could not protect the football.
cfb-2017-09-23-butler-usd: San Diego opened Pioneer Football League play with a 38–17 victory over Butler at Torero Stadium, powered by a five-touchdown afternoon from [[cfb-usd-anthony-lawrence|Anthony Lawrence]]. The quarterback completed 26 of 39 passes for 367 yards without an interception, and the Toreros amassed 499 yards of offense. The win extended San Diego's conference home winning streak to 28 games.

[[cfb-usd-justin-priest|Justin Priest]] caught nine passes for 148 yards and three touchdowns, including the game's opening score. Butler answered with two touchdown connections between [[cfb-butler-will-marty|Will Marty]] and [[cfb-butler-pace-temple|Pace Temple]], pulling within 17–14 early in the second quarter. Lawrence responded with two more touchdown passes before halftime, including a 13-yard strike to [[cfb-usd-ross-dwelley|Ross Dwelley]] with 44 seconds remaining, and San Diego carried a 31–14 lead into the break.

Butler managed only a field goal after halftime. Marty finished with 260 passing yards, and Temple caught eight passes for 155 yards and both Bulldog touchdowns. Dwelley supplied six catches for 101 yards for San Diego, while [[cfb-usd-emilio-martinez|Emilio Martinez]] ran for 93 yards, including a 52-yard fourth-quarter gain that set up the Toreros' final field goal.
cfb-2018-11-10-davidson-usd: San Diego clinched the Pioneer Football League championship and an FCS playoff berth in a breathtaking 56–52 comeback over Davidson at Torero Stadium. The Wildcats amassed an FCS-record 789 rushing yards, but [[cfb-usd-anthony-lawrence|Anthony Lawrence]] countered with a San Diego single-game record 556 passing yards and seven touchdowns. His favorite target, [[cfb-usd-michael-bandy|Michael Bandy]], caught 10 passes for a school-record 324 yards and four touchdowns.

Davidson's rushing attack looked unstoppable early. [[cfb-dav-wesley-dugger|Wesley Dugger]] broke a 94-yard touchdown run, [[cfb-dav-william-wicks|William Wicks]] scored from 90 yards out, and [[cfb-dav-keylan-brown|Keylan Brown]] added an 80-yard sprint as the Wildcats surged ahead 31–7 early in the second quarter. Lawrence kept the Toreros alive, finding Bandy, [[cfb-usd-emilio-martinez|Emilio Martinez]] and [[cfb-usd-dalton-kincaid|Dalton Kincaid]] for touchdowns as San Diego cut the deficit to 38–35 by halftime. Kincaid made two touchdown catches, while Davidson ultimately produced four 100-yard rushers: Dugger (231 yards), Wicks (197), [[cfb-dav-tyler-phelps|Tyler Phelps]] (153) and Brown (150).

After a quieter third quarter, the fourth brought another extraordinary swing. San Diego stopped Davidson on fourth-and-goal at the one after a forward-fumble ruling, and Lawrence soon connected with Bandy on a 99-yard touchdown that gave the Toreros a 49–45 lead. Brown's 12-yard scoring run put Davidson back ahead 52–49 with 2:38 left. Lawrence answered by finding Martinez for five yards, then Bandy for 46, before hitting Bandy again for the winning 20-yard touchdown with 1:43 remaining. San Diego held on to complete the comeback.

The teams combined for 1,477 yards of offense. Lawrence's seven touchdown passes tied a school record, while Davidson's 789 rushing yards broke a 30-year-old FCS record. More importantly for San Diego, the victory secured its fifth consecutive PFL championship and playoff appearance, turning one of the wildest games in program history into a title-clinching celebration.
cfb-2019-09-07-ucd-usd: UC Davis escaped Torero Stadium with a 38–35 victory over San Diego, but only after a last-second goal-line stand preserved the win. The Aggies jumped ahead 14–0 on two early touchdown passes from [[cfb-ucd-jake-maier|Jake Maier]], only for San Diego to answer with a 93-yard kickoff return and a short touchdown run by [[cfb-usd-reid-sinnett|Reid Sinnett]]. A 37-yard scoring pass from C. Crawford to Matt Hyman put UC Davis ahead 21–14 at halftime.

The teams traded touchdowns throughout the third quarter. [[cfb-usd-emilio-martinez|Emilio Martinez]] scored from 11 yards out, [[cfb-ucd-ulonzo-gilliam|Ulonzo Gilliam]] answered with a four-yard run, and Sinnett connected with [[cfb-usd-dalton-kincaid|Dalton Kincaid]] for a 20-yard touchdown to tie it at 28. Kincaid caught another Sinnett touchdown early in the fourth, giving San Diego its first lead, 35–31, with 8:47 remaining.

Gilliam then capped a 14-play, 81-yard drive with his second rushing touchdown, a one-yard run with 3:35 left, to put UC Davis ahead 38–35. San Diego drove to the doorstep of a winning score, but Devon King forced a fumble at the goal line with two seconds left, producing a touchback that sealed the Aggies' victory. Gilliam finished with 135 rushing yards and two touchdowns, Maier threw for 359 yards, and Sinnett passed for 239 yards and two touchdowns. UC Davis outgained San Diego 539–413 in a game decided on its final meaningful snap.
